issues.description: The problem statement's Part 2 requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a double parameter), but the UML, the template usage, and the provided solution define Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters. Template Main calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments and the solution's Milkable interface and implementations (Goat, Seal) use a no-argument signature. This conflicting signature will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause compilation errors if they follow the Part 2 text literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the signature mismatch: either (A) update the problem statement Part 2 to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the example return text accordingly, or (B) change the Milkable interface, its implementations (Seal, Goat), and all calls (e.g., in Main and tests) to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update the song/tests to provide a volume. Prefer option (A) if the intended design (UML and template) uses a no-arg method.

issues.description: The problem text specifies a milk method with a double parameter (messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)) and an expected return including the volume, but both the provided template usage and the solution implementation declare messageOnMilk() with no parameter. This mismatch between the problem description and the code (template/solution) creates confusion about the required method signature and what students must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() without parameters (matching the UML and existing template/solution), and revise the textual example to remove the milkVolume parameter and volume-specific return format. Alternatively, update the interface and all implementations (Milkable and classes) and template calls to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust tests/examples accordingly.
